reason: README Quick Start Method 2 evaluates a 0.5B local model on GSM8K with --limit 5, feasible on CPU with small downloads and no keys.
demo: README Quick Start, Method 2: Evaluate a Local Model (evalscope eval --datasets gsm8k arc --limit 5)
goal: Install evalscope (Python >= 3.11) and make the README Method 2 command `evalscope eval --model Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct --datasets gsm8k arc --limit 5` run to completion on CPU, with the model auto-downloaded from ModelScope and both datasets fetched. It must accept a `--work-dir <dir>` option for outputs and write the evaluation reports there.
check: The hidden test runs the local-model gsm8k + arc evaluation with limit 5 into a fresh work dir and verifies a report with a score for each dataset (5 gsm8k samples) and review files whose model answers are non-empty.

revision.by: fairness review (every maintained-set exam re-checked against the source)
issues: Too lenient: `[ -n "$rev" ] && [ "$(wc -l < "$rev")" -ge 5 ]` stays silent under set -e when the first test fails, because set -e ignores failures in an && list other than the last command. A missing reviews file therefore still prints ORACLE PASS (verified: bash -c 'set -e; rev=""; [ -n "$rev" ] && [ 1 -ge 5 ]; echo REACHED' prints REACHED).
Too lenient: the '5 evaluated samples' assertion `'"num": 5' in s or ... or 'gsm8k' in s.lower()` is always true for a gsm8k report, so the sample count is never checked.
There is no check that the model actually produced answers; a run where every generation errors could still write a report with score 0. v2 requires a non-empty assistant message in every review row.
Demo narrowed: README Method 2 is `--datasets gsm8k arc --limit 5`, and the exam dropped arc. v2 restores the README command.
The inner `timeout 5400` is longer than ORACLE_SEC=3600 (cosmetic).
